value.a: THE THREE ROLES, IN AKIEN'S WORDS (2026-07-25), and they are NOT three names for one thing NOR three things needing three system-terms: 'the callback is the tool. the poke is what the callback is doing in sending a message to get the attention of something and the verb is more or less the endpoint. the thing that will respond. the action it's going to take when it gets the poke. but we don't need that much terminology. it's just how i was using them.' So — CALLBACK is the tool (the immutable declaration, already built in cairn/tools/base/callback.py); POKE is the ACT of messaging for attention; VERB is the ENDPOINT that responds and the action it takes. This resolves rather than contradicts the collapse below: a menu of pokes IS a menu of verbs, because a poke names a verb. EXACTLY ONE noun goes on the menu — `verb` — and the other two stay as ordinary speech. Explicitly NOT minted as system terms: `handler`, `endpoint`, `dispatch table` (falsifier 10 — 'we don't need that much terminology'). BUILD CONSEQUENCE CC would otherwise have missed: `Callback` today carries `to` / `channel` / `body` — it names WHO to poke but not WHAT TO POKE. The verb belongs on the callback, so child a adds it there as well as on the envelope; a callback whose verb the target does not serve must be RED at declaration or at fire, never a silent poke into nothing.

NOT A DISTINCTION — A MENU OF VERBS AND A MENU OF POKES ARE THE SAME THING (Akien, 2026-07-25, correcting CC at n=1). CC first recorded these as two kinds — a VERB as one exchange, a CALLBACK-MENU-ITEM as a standing subscription — and Akien collapsed it. He is right, and the code already says so: `Callback` (cairn/tools/base/callback.py) carries `to` + `channel` + `body` + `why`, and `shim._fire` POSTS it — the poke IS a post. There is ONE menu (the verbs a device accepts) and ONE exchange (address + verb + envelope). `subscribe-to-cpu-threshold` is simply one verb on that menu; the callback the device wires up in response is INTERNAL — behind the device's own gate (Law 6, 'the device resolves its own method internally'), not a second public list. CONSEQUENCE, and the reason this catch matters: the split CC was holding would have built `declared_verbs()` ALONGSIDE the existing `callbacks()` — two menus, two registries, two records of what a device offers, guaranteed to drift (Law 1, the defect caught before it was written). Specimen of reify-vs-flow: CC freezes Cairn-fluid categories, Akien catches at n=1 — the fourth such specimen after rack=scheduler, ground_loop=executor, and the trigger enum.

CC'S EXTENSION OF THAT COLLAPSE, flagged as CC's inference and NOT as Akien's words: if verbs and pokes are one, then SYNC, ASYNC, and SUBSCRIPTION are not three shapes either — they are one exchange differing only in WHEN and HOW MANY replies arrive at the caller's address (wait for the correlated one / take it whenever it lands / take them repeatedly). This makes child d a parameter of the single exchange rather than a second door, which is what falsifier 4 already demanded on other grounds. Named out loud rather than smuggled in (terms drift — flag coinages); if it over-reaches the correction, it is the part to kick back.

EXTERNAL PARTICIPANTS ARE NOT ONE KIND — Akien's arrival surface is the WEB SERVER (the bus charter's filed_edge (d) names the web-server stone); CC's arrival surface is a SESSION HOOK (CC cannot be poked and does not persist between sessions). Same bus, same address, same verbs, same feed — two different ways of NOTICING. Not a special case in the substrate; an adapter at the edge.

a.distinction: CROSSING vs CHATTER vs RESIDUE — three problems, one word ('anti-bounce')
a.recorded: 2026-07-25, Akien asked 'so we need an anti-bounce?' after a durable-bus proof went red.
a.settled: The crossing half is built and proven. The other two are filed above with the specific evidence that would open each.
a.why_it_matters: They have different cures and only one was urgent. Level-flood is cured by firing on the crossing; chatter is NOT (each flap is a real crossing) and wants hysteresis; residue is neither and wants retention. Collapsing them into one word would have produced one mechanism that half-solved all three — and a damping width guessed with no measurement.

a.standing: CC coinage-by-selection, flagged for Akien's ratify.
a.why_it_matters: build-to-the-tool + falsifier 10 (a build adds no net new vocabulary). 'Edge detection' is the standard term, but this codebase already spends 'filed edge' on an open design question — overloading it costs a re-derivation on every read. 'crossing' is ALREADY native here (cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py: 'a state transition or a boundary crossing'; system_rackmount: body={'crossed': value}), so it introduces nothing and retires nothing.
